2892.h: 51 - al-Ashʿarī ʿAlī ibn Ismāʿīl ibn Isḥāq *
2892.t:
The great scholar, the imam (الإمام) of the theologians, Abū al-Ḥasan ʿAlī ibn Ismāʿīl ibn Abī Bishr Isḥāq ibn Sālim ibn Ismāʿīl ibn ʿAbd Allāh ibn Mūsā, son of the governor of Basra Bilāl ibn Abī Burdah, son of the companion of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ Abū Mūsā ʿAbd Allāh ibn Qays ibn Ḥaḍḍār al-Ashʿarī, al-Yamānī, al-Baṣrī.
His birth: in the year 260 AH, and it is said: rather he was born in the year 270. ⟦15:85⟧
He took from: أبي خليفة الجمحي، وأبي علي الجبائي، وزكريا الساجي، وسهل بن نوح، وطبقتهم، narrating from them with the chain of transmission (الإسناد) in his exegesis (التفسير) frequently.
He was a wonder in intelligence and strength of understanding.
When he excelled in knowledge of Muʿtazilism, he came to detest it and disavowed it, and went up before the people, and repented to Allah - (Exalted is He) - from it, then began to refute the Muʿtazilah (المعتزلة) and expose their defects.
The jurist (الفقيه) Abū Bakr al-Ṣayrafī said: The Muʿtazilah (المعتزلة) had raised their heads, until al-Ashʿarī arose and confined them in the cones of sesame (1) .
And from Ibn al-Bāqillānī, who said: The best of my states is that I understand the speech of al-Ashʿarī (2) .
I say: I saw four works by Abū al-Ḥasan on the fundamentals in which he mentions the principles of the school of the Salaf regarding the attributes, and he said in them: They are passed on as they came.
Then he said: And I say this, and by it I hold as my religion, and they are not interpreted.
I say: He died in Baghdad in the year 324 AH, and a group of the Ḥanbalīs and scholars attacked (4) him.
And everyone’s saying is taken and left, except the one whom Allah - (Exalted is He) - protected. O Allah, guide us and have mercy on us (5) . ⟦15:86⟧
Abū al-Ḥasan had excessive intelligence and deep immersion in knowledge, and he had fine things, and numerous works that attest to his breadth of knowledge.
Taking from him: imams (الإمام) among them: أبو الحسن الباهلي (1) ، وأبو الحسن الكرماني، وأبو زيد المروزي، وأبو عبد الله بن مجاهد البصري، وبندار بن الحسين الشيرازي، وأبو محمد العراقي، وزاهر بن أحمد السرخسي، وأبو سهل الصعلوكي، وأبو نصر الكواز (2) الشيرازي (3) .
Abū al-Ḥasan al-Ashʿarī said in his book (al-ʿUmad fī al-Ruʾyah) : I compiled (al-Fuṣūl fī al-Radd ʿalā al-Mulḥidīn) , which is twelve books, and the book (al-Mūjaz) , and the book (Khalq al-Aʿmāl) , and the book (al-Ṣifāt) , which is large, in which we spoke about the sects of the Muʿtazilah (المعتزلة) and the Jahmiyyah (الجهمية), and the book (al-Ruʾyah bi-al-Abṣār) , and the book (al-Khāṣṣ wa-al-ʿĀmm) , and the book (al-Radd ʿalā al-Mujassimah) , and the book (Īḍāḥ al-Burhān) , and the book (al-Lumaʿ fī al-Radd ʿalā Ahl al-Bidaʿ) , and the book (al-Sharḥ wa-al-Tafṣīl) , and the book (al-Naqḍ ʿalā al-Jubbāʾī (4)) , and the book (al-Naqḍ ʿalā al-Balkhī (5)) , and the book (Jumal Maqālāt al-Mulḥidīn) , and a book (6) on the attributes which is the greatest of our books, in which we refuted what we had composed long ago on it to establish the doctrine of the Muʿtazilah, ⟦15:87⟧ no book like it having been composed for them; then Allah made the truth clear to us, and we returned.
And a book (al-Radd ʿalā Ibn al-Rāwandī) , and the book (al-Qāmiʿ fī al-Radd ʿalā al-Khālidī) , and the book (Adab al-Jadal) , and the book (Jawāb al-Khurāsāniyyah) , and the book (Jawāb al-Sīrāfiyyīn) , and (Jawāb al-Jurjāniyyīn) , and the book (al-Masāʾil al-Manthūrah al-Baghdādiyyah) , and the book (al-Funūn fī al-Radd ʿalā al-Mulḥidīn) , and the book (al-Nawādir fī Daqāʾiq al-Kalām) and the book (Tafsīr al-Qurʾān) .
And he named many other books besides that.
Then after (al-ʿUmad) he composed several books which Ibn Fūrak named, and they are in (Tabyīn Kadhib al-Muftarī (1)) .
I saw a saying of al-Ashʿarī that pleased me, and it is established, narrated by al-Bayhaqī: I heard Abū Ḥāzim al-ʿAbdawī, I heard Zāhir ibn Aḥmad al-Sarakhsī say: When the appointed time of Abū al-Ḥasan al-Ashʿarī drew near, in my house in Baghdad, he called me and I came to him, and he said: Bear witness against me that I do not declare any of the people of the qiblah to be an unbeliever, because all of them point to one object of worship, and all of this is merely a difference of expressions.
I say: And I hold something like this as my religion, and so our shaykh Ibn Taymiyyah, in the last of his days, used to say: I do not declare anyone (2) of the Ummah to be an unbeliever, and he would say:
The Prophet ﷺ said: “None maintains ablution except a believer (3)” so whoever keeps up the prayers with ablution is a Muslim. ⟦15:88⟧
al-Ahwāzī (1) composed a treatise on the faults of Ibn Abī Bishr, in which there are falsehoods.
And Abū al-Qāsim collected benefits in his virtues, some of which are also not authentic (الصحيح), and he has the famous debate with al-Jubbāʾī on their saying: It is obligatory on Allah to do what is most beneficial. al-Ashʿarī said: Rather He does what He wills (2) . What do you say about three children: one of them died, and two grew up, one of them believed and the other disbelieved; what is the reason for the cutting short of the child?
He said: Because He - (Exalted is He) - knew that had he reached maturity he would have disbelieved, so cutting him short was better for him.
al-Ashʿarī said: But He gave life to one of them, and he disbelieved.
He said: He only gave him life so as to expose him to the highest ranks.
al-Ashʿarī said: Then why was the child not given life so as to expose him to the highest ranks?
al-Jubbāʾī said: You are suffering whisperings.
He said: No, by Allah, but the shaykh’s donkey has come to a halt.
It has reached us that Abū al-Ḥasan repented and went up the pulpit of Basra and said: I used to say: in the creation of the Qurʾān (خلق القرآن), and that Allah is not seen with the eyes (3) , and that evil is my act and not by decree, and I am repentant, holding firmly to the refutation of the Muʿtazilah (المعتزلة) (4) .
There was in him joking and much humour.
Ibn Khallikān said it (5) .
And he wrote many books, and he was content with little, and he had a share of a village from the endowment (الوقف) of their grandfather ⟦15:89⟧ the governor Bilāl ibn Abī Burdah (1) .
And it is said: He remained alive until the year 330 AH.

4149.h: 73 - Ibn Bundār ʿAbd al-Raḥmān ibn Aḥmad ibn al-Ḥasan al-ʿIjlī *
4149.t:
The Imam (الإمام), the exemplar (القدوة), Shaykh al-Islām (شيخ الإسلام), Abū al-Faḍl ʿAbd al-Raḥmān, son of the hadith scholar (المحدث) Aḥmad ibn al-Ḥasan ibn Bundār al-ʿIjlī, al-Rāzī, Meccan by birth, the Qurʾān reciter (المقرئ).
He recited the Qurʾān under Abū ʿAbd Allāh al-Mujāhidī, a student of Ibn Mujāhid, and recited with the reading of Ibn ⟦18:135⟧ ʿĀmir under the Qurʾān reciter (المقرئ) of Damascus ʿAlī ibn Dāwūd al-Dārānī, and recited in Baghdad under Abū al-Ḥasan al-Ḥammāmī, and a group.
And he heard in Mecca from: أحمد بن فراس، وعلي بن جعفر السيرواني الزاهد، ووالده أبي العباس بن بندار، and in Rayy from: جعفر بن فناكي.
And in Baghdad from: أبي الحسن الرفاء، وعدة.
And in Damascus from: عبد الوهاب الكلابي.
And in Isfahan from: أبي عبد الله بن مندة.
And in Basra, Kufa, Ḥarrān, Tustar, al-Ruhā, Fasā, Homs, Egypt, al-Ramlah, Nishapur, Nasā, and Jurjān, and he travelled the horizons for most of his life, and he was one of the unique ones of the age in knowledge and deed.
Taking from him: المستغفري (1) أحد شيوخه، وأبو بكر الخطيب، وأبو صالح المؤذن، ونصر بن محمد الشيرازي؛ شيخ للسلفي، وأبو علي الحداد، ومحمد بن عبد الواحد الدقاق، والحسين بن عبد الملك الخلال، وأبو سهل بن سعدويه، وفاطمة بنت البغدادي، وخلق.
And in Egypt he met Abū Muslim the scribe (2) .
ʿAbd al-Ghāfir ibn Ismāʿīl said: He was reliable (ثقة), a traveller, an imam (الإمام) in the recitation traditions (القراءات), unique in his way; the shaykhs revered him, and he did not reside in the Sufi lodges (الخانقاه), but would take refuge in a ruined mosque, and when his place became known he would move away, and he would not take anything from anyone, and if something was opened to him he would give preference with it to others (3) .
And Yaḥyā ibn Mandah said: A group recited the Qurʾān to him, and he left us for ⟦18:136⟧ Kirmān, and narrated hadith there.
He died in the town of Ūshīr: in Jumādā al-Ūlā in the year 454 AH.
He said: And he was born in the year 371 AH, and he is reliable (ثقة), scrupulous, devout in religion, acquainted with the recitation traditions (القراءات), learned in literature and grammar; he is greater than someone like me can point to, and more renowned than the sun, and brighter than the moon, possessor of arts of knowledge, awe-inspiring and looked up to, eloquent, of good conduct, of great weight (1) .
al-Silafī said: I heard ʿAbd al-Salām ibn Salamah in Marand (2) say: Abū al-Faḍl al-Rāzī followed al-Sayrawānī, the shaykh of the Sanctuary, and al-Sayrawānī accompanied Abū Muḥammad al-Murtaʿish (3) , the companion of al-Junayd.
And al-Khallāl said: Abū al-Faḍl the Imam (الإمام) set out toward Kirmān, and the people escorted him, and he sent them back, and made for the road alone, saying:
If we travel by night with you as our imam (الإمام) ... the remembrance of you is enough as a driver for our mounts (4)
al-Khallāl said: And he recited to me one of his own:
O death, how harsh a visitor you are ... you descend upon a man against his will
And you take the maiden from her chamber ... and you take the only son from his mother
al-Samʿānī said in (al-Dhayl) : He was an excellent Qurʾān reciter (المقرئ), the author of many works, ⟦18:137⟧ of good conduct, an ascetic (الزاهد), devoted in worship, austere in living, solitary, content, giving recitation instruction and hearing hadith for most of his time, and he would travel alone and enter the deserts (1) .
I read to Isḥāq al-Asadī: أخبرنا ابن خليل، أخبرنا خليل بن بدر، أخبرنا محمد بن عبد الواحد الدقاق قال:
The unique Imam (الإمام) Abū al-Faḍl al-Rāzī came to us - may Allah grant him His pleasure and settle him in His gardens - and he was an imam (الإمام) among the reliable (ثقة) imams (الإمام) in hadith, narrations, the Sunnah (السنة) and the verses; mention of him fills the mouth and makes the eye pour tears; he came to Isfahan several times; I heard a good portion from him; he was an awe-inspiring man, tall of stature, a friend of Allah among the friends of Allah, a man of karāmāt, who travelled the world benefiting others and being benefited (2) .
al-Khallāl said: Abū al-Faḍl was on a road, with bread and fānīdh (3) with him, and highway robbers wanted to take it from him, so he drove them off with his staff; he was asked about that, and he said: Because it was lawful, and perhaps I would not find the like of it (4) .
And he entered Kirmān in a shabby appearance, in worn tatters and rags, and he was brought to the king, and they said: A spy.
The king said: What is the news?
He said: Do you ask me about the news of the earth or the news of the heavens? If you are asking me about the news of the heavens, then “Every day He is engaged in some affair” [Qurʾān 55:29] and if you are asking me about the news of the earth, then “Everyone upon it will perish” [Qurʾān 55:26] and the king marvelled at his words, and honoured him, and offered him wealth, but he did not accept it (5) . ⟦18:138⟧

3117.h: 274 - al-Ṣibghī Aḥmad ibn Isḥāq ibn Ayyūb al-Naysābūrī *
3117.t:
The Imam (الإمام), the great scholar, the mufti (المفتي), the hadith scholar (المحدث), Shaykh al-Islām (شيخ الإسلام), Abū Bakr Aḥmad ibn Isḥāq ibn Ayyūb ibn Yazīd al-Naysābūrī, al-Shāfiʿī, known as: al-Ṣibghī (3) .
His birth: in the year 258 AH. ⟦15:483⟧
He saw Yaḥyā ibn Muḥammad al-Dhuhlī, and Abū Ḥātim al-Rāzī.
He heard from: الفضل بن محمد الشعراني، وإسماعيل بن قتيبة، ويوسف بن يعقوب القزويني، والحارث بن أبي أسامة، وهشام بن علي السيرافي، وعلي بن عبد العزيز البغوي، وإسماعيل القاضي، ومحمد بن أيوب البجلي وطبقتهم بنيسابور والحجاز والبصرة وبغداد والري.
He compiled and authored, excelled in jurisprudence (الفقه), and distinguished himself in the science of hadith.
He performed the pilgrimage in the year 283, and Abū al-Qāsim al-Baghawī read to his uncle for him (Muntaqā al-Musnad) .
Narrating from him: حمزة بن محمد الزيدي، وأبو علي الحافظ، وأبو أحمد الحاكم، وأبو بكر الإسماعيلي، ومحمد بن إبراهيم الجرجاني، وأبو عبد الله الحاكم، وخلق كثير.
al-Ḥākim said: I heard him say: When I reached adolescence I busied myself with learning horsemanship, and I did not hear a single letter, and I was taken to Rayy while Abū Ḥātim was alive, and I asked him about a question regarding my father’s inheritance; then we returned to Nishapur in the year 280 AH, and while I was at the door of our house, with Abū Ḥāmid ibn al-Sharqī and Abū Ḥāmid ibn Ḥasnawayh sitting, they said to me: Busy yourself with the direct hearing (السماع) of hadith.
I said: From whom?
They said: From Ismāʿīl ibn Qutaybah.
So I went to him, and heard, and became eager for hadith, then left for Iraq a year later.
al-Ḥākim said: The Imam (الإمام) Abū Bakr remained issuing legal opinions in Nishapur for fifty-odd years, and no question was held against him in his legal opinions (الفتوى) in which he had erred (1) .
And he has the extensive books such as (al-Ṭahārah) , ⟦15:484⟧ and (al-Ṣalāh) , and (al-Zakāh) , and so on to the end of the book (al-Mabsūṭ) .
I heard Abū al-Faḍl ibn Ibrāhīm say:
Abū Bakr ibn Isḥāq used to deputise for the Imam (الإمام) of the imams (الإمام), Ibn Khuzaymah, in giving legal opinions (الفتوى) for over ten years, in the Great Mosque and elsewhere.
Then al-Ḥākim said: I heard the Shaykh Abū Bakr say: I saw in my sleep as if I were in a house in which was ʿUmar, and the people had gathered around him asking him questions; he gestured to me to answer them; and I kept asking and answering, while he was saying to me:
You are right, proceed; you are right, proceed.
So I said: O Commander of the Faithful (أمير المؤمنين), what is the salvation from the world, or the way out of it?
He said to me with his finger: Supplication; and I repeated the question to him, and he gathered himself as if prostrating in his humility, then said: Supplication.
al-Ḥākim said: Among his works are the book (al-Asmāʾ wa-al-Ṣifāt) , and the book (al-Īmān) , and the book (al-Qadar) , and the book (al-Khulafāʾ al-Arbaʿah) , and the book (al-Ruʾyah) , and the book (al-Aḥkām) - it was carried to Baghdad, and praise of it was abundant - meaning: this composition -, and the book (al-Imāmah) .
And I heard him addressing a middle-aged man from the people of (1) , and he said: They narrated to us from Sulaymān ibn Ḥarb, and he said to him: Spare us “they narrated to us”; how long will it be “they narrated to us” and “they informed us”?
So he said: O you, I do not smell the scent of faith in your speech, and it is not permissible for you to enter this house; then he shunned him until he died.
al-Ḥākim said: I heard Muḥammad ibn Ḥamdūn say: I accompanied Abū Bakr ibn Isḥāq for years, and I never saw him omit the night prayer, neither on a journey nor at home (2) . ⟦15:485⟧
I saw Abū Bakr more than once, after the call to prayer, supplicating and weeping, and sometimes he would strike his head against the wall, until one day I feared that his head would bleed, and I never saw among our group of shaykhs anyone with a finer prayer than his, and he would not allow anyone to backbite in his gathering (1) .
And I heard him more than once, when he recited a verse of poetry, spoil it and alter it until the metre was lost, and his intellect (2) and judgment were proverbial.
And he was asked about someone who catches the bowing without having recited al-Fātiḥah, and he said: He repeats the rakʿah (3) .
Then al-Ḥākim said: حدثنا أبو بكر بن إسحاق، حدثنا يوسف بن يعقوب القزويني، حدثنا سعيد بن يحيى الأصبهاني، حدثنا سعير بن الخمس، عن أبي إسحاق، عن أبي الأحوص، عن عبد الله، قال:
Whoever loves to meet Allah tomorrow as a Muslim, let him keep up these five prayers wherever the call is made for them.
al-Ḥākim said: al-Dāraquṭnī wrote this down from me, and said: I have never written it down from anyone.
And al-Khalīlī narrated it from al-Ḥākim, and al-Khalīlī said: And Ibn Mandah narrated it from al-Ṣibghī.
And Ibn Mandah said: Abū al-Shaykh the hadith master (الحافظ) wrote it down from me.
A group narrated it from al-Hajarī.
And nothing came from Saʿīr except by this route, from Abū Isḥāq, and he is Ibrāhīm al-Hajarī (4) and not al-Sabīʿī; then al-Khalīlī went to great lengths in glorifying him. ⟦15:486⟧
al-Ḥākim said: And I heard Abū Bakr ibn Isḥāq say:
We left the session of Ibrāhīm al-Ḥarbī, and with us was a man of much frivolity, and he saw a beardless youth, and stepped forward and said:
Peace be upon you, and shook his hand, and kissed his eyes and his cheek, then said: al-Dabarī narrated to us in Ṣanʿāʾ with his chain of transmission (الإسناد), saying:
The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: “When one of you loves his brother, let him inform him (1)” .
So I said to him: Are you not ashamed, committing sodomy and lying in hadith?
Meaning: that he fabricated a chain of transmission (الإسناد) for the text.
al-Ṣibghī died in Shaʿbān in the year 342 AH.
And dying in the same year were: the musnid (المسند) of Hamadan Abū Jaʿfar Aḥmad ibn ʿUbayd al-Asadī; the shaykh of the Sufis (الصوفي) Ibrāhīm ibn al-Mawlid; the musnid (المسند) Abū al-Faḍl al-Ḥasan ibn Yaʿqūb al-Bukhārī; the musnid (المسند) ʿAbd al-Raḥmān ibn Ḥamdān al-Jallāb in Hamadan; the judge (القاضي), the great scholar Abū al-Qāsim ʿAlī ibn Muḥammad ibn Abī al-Fahm al-Tanūkhī; the shaykh of Merv, the Imam (الإمام) Abū al-ʿAbbās al-Qāsim ibn al-Qāsim ibn Mahdī al-Sayyārī, grandson of Aḥmad ibn Sayyār ⟦15:487⟧ the hadith master (الحافظ); the musnid (المسند) Abū al-Ḥusayn Muḥammad ibn Aḥmad ibn Muḥammad ibn ʿAlī al-Aswārī al-Aṣbahānī; and the shaykh of the hadith scholars (المحدث) and ascetics (الزاهد) in Nishapur Abū Bakr Muḥammad ibn Dāwūd ibn Sulaymān al-Naysābūrī.
I read to Abū al-Maʿālī Aḥmad ibn al-Muʾayyad: أخبرنا محمد بن محمد المأموني، أخبرنا أحمد بن محمد الحافظ، أخبرنا القاسم بن الفضل، حدثنا محمد بن إبراهيم بن جعفر اليزدي إملاء، أخبرنا أبو بكر أحمد بن إسحاق بن أيوب الصبغي، حدثنا محمد بن غالب بن حرب، حدثنا داود بن عبد الله الجعفري، حدثنا مالك عن نافع:
عن ابن عمر that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ used to raise his hands when he said the takbīr, and when he raised (1) .
And by the same chain: أخبرنا الصبغي، حدثنا أحمد بن القاسم بن أبي مساور، حدثنا أبو معمر إسماعيل بن إبراهيم قال:
Ibn Wahb dictated to me from his memory, عن يونس، عن الزهري:
عن أنس that the Prophet ﷺ said: “There is no amputation for the plunderer, nor the snatcher, nor the embezzler” (2) . ⟦15:488⟧
Very gharīb (الغريب).
Despite the probity of its narrators, one should not narrate except from a book, for I see that Ibn Wahb, despite his memory, erred in it, and the text has a chain of transmission (الإسناد) other than this.
His brother:

5582.h: 156 - Ibn Baqī Aḥmad ibn Yazīd ibn ʿAbd al-Raḥmān al-Umawī *
5582.t:
The Imam (الإمام), the great scholar, the hadith scholar (المحدث), the musnid (المسند), the judge (القاضي) of the community, Abū al-Qāsim Aḥmad, son of Abū al-Walīd Yazīd ibn ʿAbd al-Raḥmān ibn Aḥmad ibn Muḥammad ibn Aḥmad ibn Makhlad ibn ʿAbd ⟦22:274⟧ al-Raḥmān ibn Aḥmad, son of the shaykh of Andalusia, the hadith master (الحافظ) Baqī ibn Makhlad, al-Umawī, their client (المولى), al-Baqawī, al-Qurṭubī, al-Mālikī.
He heard from: أباه، وجده؛ أبا الحسن، ومحمد بن عبد الحق الخزرجي صاحب محمد بن الفرج الطلاعي، وخلف بن بشكوال، وأبا زيد السهيلي (1) ، وطائفة.
Those who gave him a licence to transmit (الإجازة): المقرئ أبو الحسن شريح بن محمد، وعبد الملك بن مسرة.
He was unique in transmitting certain things, among them (Muwaṭṭaʾ Yaḥyā ibn Yaḥyā) , from al-Khazrajī.
And he and all his forefathers narrated hadith.
Abū ʿAbd Allāh al-Abbār (2) said: He is one of the great men of Andalusia in eminence and perfection; we do not know of a house more deeply rooted in knowledge and distinction than his house, except the house of Banū Mughīth in Cordoba and Banū al-Bājī in Seville, and he is ahead of these; he held the judgeship of the community in Marrakesh, in addition to the offices of redress of grievances and chief secretaryship, and his conduct was praised, and the elevation only increased him in humility; then he was dismissed, and remained unemployed (3) until he was appointed to the judgeship of his town, and went there, then was dismissed before his death, and the students crowded around him, and he deserved that.
And Ibn al-Zubayr - or another - said: He had a long reach in grammar and literature; people competed to take from him, and he read the whole of (Kitāb Sībawayh) to Abū al-ʿAbbās ibn Maḍāʾ, and read (al-Maqāmāt) to him.
And Ibn Musdī said: This shaykh of ours was the leader in the two Maghribs, and he held the judgeship of the two banks, and when he grew old he asked to be excused, and returned to his town, and remained judge (القاضي) there until ⟦22:275⟧ old age overcame him, so he stayed in his house; and he was knowledgeable about consensus (الإجماع) and juristic disagreement (الخلاف), inclined to preference and fairness.
I say: The long-lived Abū Muḥammad ibn Hārūn narrated from him, who wrote to us with the licence to transmit (الإجازة) from the Maghrib, and a group.
Narrating from him with the licence to transmit (الإجازة): محمد بن عياش الخزرجي، والخطيب أبو القاسم بن الأيسر الجذامي، وأبو الحكم مالك بن المرحل الأديب، وآخرون.
And he - (may Allah have mercy on him) - was predominantly inclined, in his affairs and rulings, to the way of the people of tradition and of the literal meaning.
Among those narrating from him: العلامة أبو الحسين بن أبي الربيع، وبالإجازة: محمد بن محمد المومنائي الفاسي.
أخبرنا عبد الله بن محمد بن هارون الطائي الفقيه إذنا، قال: أنبأنا أحمد بن يزيد القاضي، عن شريح بن محمد المقرئ، عن الفقيه أبي محمد بن حزم، أخبرنا يحيى بن عبد الرحمن، أخبرنا قاسم بن أصبغ، حدثنا إبراهيم بن عبد الله العبسي، حدثنا وكيع، عن الأعمش، عن أبي صالح، عن أبي هريرة، قال:
The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: “Fasting is a shield (1)” .
Ibn Baqī was born in the year 537 AH.
And he died: on Friday, after the prayer, in mid-Ramaḍān, in the year 625 AH, in Cordoba, having passed eighty-eight years of age - (may Allah have mercy on him) - and he was the last ⟦22:276⟧ person in the world to narrate (al-Muwaṭṭaʾ) with an elevated chain (العالي) between him and the Imam (الإمام) Mālik, in which there are six men with continuous direct hearing (السماع), and such is the number in (al-Muwaṭṭaʾ) of Yaḥyā ibn Bukayr for Mukram ibn Abī al-Ṣaqr al-Bazzāz, and in (Muwaṭṭaʾ al-Qaʿnabī) for the Muwaffaqs: Ibn Qudāmah and ʿAbd al-Laṭīf, and Ibn al-Khayr, and in (Muwaṭṭaʾ Abī Muṣʿab) for Abū Naṣr ibn al-Shīrāzī and Ibn al-Burhān, and in (Muwaṭṭaʾ Suwayd ibn Saʿīd) for al-Bahāʾ ʿAbd al-Raḥmān.
